sanskrit: duḥsahasyaitad ābhāti śarīraṃ saṃvṛtaṃ śaraiḥ girir ātmaruhaiḥ phullaiḥ karṇikārair ivāvṛtaḥ
english: This body of the indomitable one, sheathed in arrows, shines like a mountain covered with its own flowering karṇikāra trees in full bloom.

sanskrit: śātakaumbhyā srajā bhāti kavacena ca bhāsvatā agnineva giriḥ śveto gatāsur api duḥsahaḥ
english: With his golden garland and his gleaming armor he shines like a white mountain crowned with fire; though his life has fled, he is hard to look upon, unconquerable still.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca adhyardhaguṇam āhur yaṃ bale śaurye ca mādhava pitrā tvayā ca dāśārha dṛptaṃ siṃham ivotkaṭam
english: Gāndhārī said: Him whom they declared, O Mādhava, to surpass by half his father and you yourself, O Dāśārha, in strength and in valor — fierce as a proud, towering lion —

sanskrit: yo bibheda camūm eko mama putrasya durbhidām sa bhūtvā mṛtyur anyeṣāṃ svayaṃ mṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: who alone shattered my son's army that none could pierce — he, having become death to others, has himself passed into the power of death.

sanskrit: tasyopalakṣaye kṛṣṇa kārṣṇer amitatejasaḥ abhimanyor hatasyāpi prabhā naivopaśāmyati
english: Even now, O Kṛṣṇa, I see that the radiance of Abhimanyu, son of Arjuna, of immeasurable splendor, does not fade though he is slain.

sanskrit: eṣā virāṭaduhitā snuṣā gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ ārtā bālā patiṃ vīraṃ śocyā śocaty aninditā
english: This daughter of Virāṭa, the daughter-in-law of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva — a young girl, grief-stricken and blameless, pitiable herself — mourns her hero husband.

sanskrit: tam eṣā hi samāsādya bhāryā bhartāram antike virāṭaduhitā kṛṣṇa pāṇinā parimārjati
english: For drawing close to him, O Kṛṣṇa, this wife, the daughter of Virāṭa, strokes her husband beside her with her hand.

sanskrit: tasya vaktram upāghrāya saubhadrasya yaśasvinī vibuddhakamalākāraṃ kambuvṛttaśirodharam
english: Kissing the face of the son of Subhadrā, that glorious woman — his face shaped like a full-blown lotus, his neck rounded like a conch —

sanskrit: kāmyarūpavatī caiṣā pariṣvajati bhāminī lajjamānā purevainaṃ mādhvīkamadamūrchitā
english: and this lovely, desirable woman embraces him, bashful as before, as if swooning with the wine of love.

sanskrit: tasya kṣatajasaṃdigdhaṃ jātarūpapariṣkṛtam vimucya kavacaṃ kṛṣṇa śarīram abhivīkṣate
english: Loosening his gold-adorned armor, smeared with blood, O Kṛṣṇa, she gazes upon his body.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇā taṃ bālā kṛṣṇa tvām abhibhāṣate ayaṃ te puṇḍarīkākṣa sadṛśākṣo nipātitaḥ
english: Gazing upon him, the young girl speaks to you, O Kṛṣṇa: 'Here, O lotus-eyed one, lies struck down he whose eyes were the equal of yours.'

sanskrit: bale vīrye ca sadṛśas tejasā caiva te 'nagha rūpeṇa ca tavātyarthaṃ śete bhuvi nipātitaḥ
english: 'Your equal in strength and valor and splendor, O sinless one, and surpassingly like you in beauty, he lies cast down upon the earth.'

sanskrit: atyantasukumārasya rāṅkavājinaśāyinaḥ kaccid adya śarīraṃ te bhūmau na paritapyate
english: 'You who were so very delicate, who lay on the finest deerskin spreads — does your body now feel no anguish upon the bare ground?'

sanskrit: mātaṅgabhujavarṣmāṇau jyākṣepakaṭhinatvacau kāñcanāṅgadinau śeṣe nikṣipya vipulau bhujau
english: 'You lie flinging out your two broad arms, thick as an elephant's trunk, their skin hardened by the bowstring's snap, banded with gold.'

sanskrit: vyāyamya bahudhā nūnaṃ sukhasuptaḥ śramād iva evaṃ vilapatīm ārtāṃ na hi mām abhibhāṣase
english: 'Surely, having labored long in many ways, you sleep at ease as if from weariness; for thus to me, lamenting and stricken, you make no answer.'

sanskrit: āryām ārya subhadrāṃ tvam imāṃś ca tridaśopamān pitṝn māṃ caiva duḥkhārtāṃ vihāya kva gamiṣyasi
english: 'O noble one, abandoning the noble Subhadrā, and these your fathers who are like the gods, and me too, worn with grief — where will you go?'

sanskrit: tasya śoṇitasaṃdigdhān keśān unnāmya pāṇinā utsaṅge vaktram ādhāya jīvantam iva pṛcchati svasrīyaṃ vāsudevasya putraṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: Lifting his blood-soaked hair with her hand and laying his face in her lap, she questions him as though he lived — the sister's son of Vāsudeva, the son of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva:

sanskrit: kathaṃ tvāṃ raṇamadhyasthaṃ jaghnur ete mahārathāḥ dhig astu krūrakartṝṃs tān kṛpakarṇajayadrathān
english: 'How did these great chariot-warriors slay you as you stood in the thick of battle? Shame upon those cruel doers — Kṛpa, Karṇa, Jayadratha,'

sanskrit: droṇadrauṇāyanī cobhau yair asi vyasanīkṛtaḥ ratharṣabhāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ katham āsīt tadā manaḥ
english: 'and Droṇa and the son of Droṇa, both — those by whom you were brought to ruin! What then was the conscience of all those bulls among chariot-warriors?'

sanskrit: bālaṃ tvāṃ parivāryaikaṃ mama duḥkhāya jaghnuṣām kathaṃ nu pāṇḍavānāṃ ca pāñcālānāṃ ca paśyatām tvaṃ vīra nidhanaṃ prāpto nāthavān sannanāthavat
english: 'They surrounded you, a lone boy, and slew you to my sorrow. How, O hero, before the very eyes of the Pāṇḍavas and the Pāñcālas, did you meet your death — protected, yet as though you had no protector?'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bahubhir ākrande nihataṃ tvām anāthavat vīraḥ puruṣaśārdūlaḥ kathaṃ jīvati pāṇḍavaḥ
english: 'Having seen you slain by many in the battle's roar, as though defenseless, how does the heroic Pāṇḍava, that tiger among men, go on living?'

sanskrit: na rājyalābho vipulaḥ śatrūṇāṃ vā parābhavaḥ prītiṃ dāsyati pārthānāṃ tvām ṛte puṣkarekṣaṇa
english: 'Not the winning of a vast kingdom, nor the rout of their foes, will give joy to the sons of Pṛthā without you, O lotus-eyed one.'

sanskrit: tava śastrajitāṃl lokān dharmeṇa ca damena ca kṣipram anvāgamiṣyāmi tatra māṃ pratipālaya
english: 'To those worlds you have won by your weapons, by righteousness and self-restraint, I shall swiftly follow you — wait for me there.'

sanskrit: durmaraṃ punar aprāpte kāle bhavati kena cit yad ahaṃ tvāṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā hataṃ jīvāmi durbhagā
english: 'Hard it is for anyone to die before the appointed hour has come — for I, ill-fated, still live, though I have seen you slain in battle.'

sanskrit: kām idānīṃ naravyāghra ślakṣṇayā smitayā girā pitṛloke sametyānyāṃ mām ivāmantrayiṣyasi
english: 'What other woman, O tiger among men, meeting her in the world of the fathers, will you now address as you addressed me, with smiling, gentle speech?'

sanskrit: nūnam apsarasāṃ svarge manāṃsi pramathiṣyasi parameṇa ca rūpeṇa girā ca smitapūrvayā
english: 'Surely in heaven you will set the hearts of the apsarases astir with your surpassing beauty and your smiling words.'

sanskrit: prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃl lokān apsarobhiḥ sameyivān saubhadra viharan kāle smarethāḥ sukṛtāni me
english: 'Having gained the worlds of those who have done good deeds, joined with the apsarases, sporting there in time, O son of Subhadrā, remember my devotion to you.'

sanskrit: etāvān iha saṃvāso vihitas te mayā saha ṣaṇmāsān saptame māsi tvaṃ vīra nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: 'Only this much fellowship with me was ordained for you here: six months, and in the seventh, O hero, you went to your death.'

sanskrit: ity uktavacanām etām apakarṣanti duḥkhitām uttarāṃ moghasaṃkalpāṃ matsyarājakulastriyaḥ
english: As she spoke these words, grief-stricken and her hopes brought to nothing, the women of the house of the Matsya king draw Uttarā away.

sanskrit: uttarām apakṛṣyainām ārtām ārtatarāḥ svayam virāṭaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā krośanti vilapanti ca
english: Drawing away the stricken Uttarā, themselves more stricken still, they cry aloud and lament when they behold Virāṭa slain.

sanskrit: droṇāstraśarasaṃkṛttaṃ śayānaṃ rudhirokṣitam virāṭaṃ vitudanty ete gṛdhragomāyuvāyasāḥ
english: Virāṭa lies torn by the arrows of Droṇa's weapon, drenched in blood, and these vultures, jackals, and crows tear at him.

sanskrit: vitudyamānaṃ vihagair virāṭam asitekṣaṇāḥ na śaknuvanti vivaśā nivartayitum āturāḥ
english: As Virāṭa is torn by the birds, the dark-eyed women, helpless and distraught, are unable to drive them off.

sanskrit: āsām ātapataptānām āyāsena ca yoṣitām śrameṇa ca vivarṇānāṃ rūpāṇāṃ vigataṃ vapuḥ
english: From these women, scorched by the sun and pale with toil and weariness, the bloom of their beauty has fled.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ cābhimanyuṃ ca kāmbojaṃ ca sudakṣiṇam śiśūn etān hatān paśya lakṣmaṇaṃ ca sudarśanam āyodhanaśiromadhye śayānaṃ paśya mādhava
english: Behold these youths slain — Uttara and Abhimanyu and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja — and behold too the fair Lakṣmaṇa lying amid the forefront of the battlefield, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca eṣa vaikartanaḥ śete maheṣvāso mahārathaḥ jvalitānalavat saṃkhye saṃśāntaḥ pārthatejasā
english: Gāndhārī said: Here lies Vaikartana, the mighty archer, the great chariot-warrior, who blazed in battle like a kindled fire, now quenched by the splendor of Pārtha.

sanskrit: paśya vaikartanaṃ karṇaṃ nihatyātirathān bahūn śoṇitaughaparītāṅgaṃ śayānaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi
english: Behold Karṇa, son of the Sun, who slew many supreme warriors — his limbs awash with floods of blood, fallen and lying upon the ground.

sanskrit: amarṣī dīrgharoṣaś ca maheṣvāso mahārathaḥ raṇe vinihataḥ śete śūro gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Impatient of insult and long-wrathful, the mighty archer, the great chariot-warrior, that hero lies slain in battle by the wielder of Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: yaṃ sma pāṇḍavasaṃtrāsān mama putrā mahārathāḥ prāyudhyanta puraskṛtya mātaṅgā iva yūthapam
english: He whom my sons, the great chariot-warriors, set before them and fought behind, in their dread of the Pāṇḍavas, as elephants rally behind the leader of the herd —

sanskrit: śārdūlam iva siṃhena samare savyasācinā mātaṅgam iva mattena mātaṅgena nipātitam
english: struck down in battle by Savyasācin as a tiger is struck down by a lion, as a rutting elephant is felled by another elephant.

sanskrit: sametāḥ puruṣavyāghra nihataṃ śūram āhave prakīrṇamūrdhajāḥ patnyo rudatyaḥ paryupāsate
english: His wives, gathered round, O tiger among men, their hair disheveled, weeping, sit beside the hero slain in battle.

sanskrit: udvignaḥ satataṃ yasmād dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ trayodaśa samā nidrāṃ cintayann nādhyagacchata
english: He on whose account the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira was forever troubled, and for thirteen years, brooding, could not find sleep —

sanskrit: anādhṛṣyaḥ parair yuddhe śatrubhir maghavān iva yugāntāgnir ivārciṣmān himavān iva ca sthiraḥ
english: unassailable by his foes in battle, like Maghavan among his enemies; blazing like the fire at the end of an age; steadfast as the Himālaya —

sanskrit: sa bhūtvā śaraṇaṃ vīro dhārtarāṣṭrasya mādhava bhūmau vinihataḥ śete vātarugṇa iva drumaḥ
english: that hero, having become the refuge of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, O Mādhava, lies slain upon the earth like a tree broken by the wind.

sanskrit: paśya karṇasya patnīṃ tvaṃ vṛṣasenasya mātaram lālapyamānāḥ karuṇaṃ rudatīṃ patitāṃ bhuvi
english: Behold the wife of Karṇa, the mother of Vṛṣasena, wailing piteously, weeping, fallen to the ground.

sanskrit: ācāryaśāpo 'nugato dhruvaṃ tvāṃ; yad agrasac cakram iyaṃ dharā te tataḥ śareṇāpahṛtaṃ śiras te; dhanaṃjayenāhave śatrumadhye
english: Surely the teacher's curse pursued you, in that this earth swallowed your chariot-wheel; and then your head was carried off by Dhanaṃjaya's arrow in battle, amid the foe.

sanskrit: aho dhig eṣā patitā visaṃjñā; samīkṣya jāmbūnadabaddhaniṣkam karṇaṃ mahābāhum adīnasattvaṃ; suṣeṇamātā rudatī bhṛśārtā
english: Alas! Beholding the mighty-armed Karṇa of undaunted spirit, his breast-plate bound with gold, the mother of Suṣeṇa, weeping and sorely stricken, has fallen senseless.

sanskrit: alpāvaśeṣo hi kṛto mahātmā; śarīrabhakṣaiḥ paribhakṣayadbhiḥ draṣṭuṃ na saṃprītikaraḥ śaśīva; kṛṣṇaśya pakṣasya caturdaśāhe
english: For little is left of that great soul, devoured by the eaters of corpses; he is no gladdening sight to look upon, like the moon on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.

sanskrit: sāvartamānā patitā pṛthivyām; utthāya dīnā punar eva caiṣā karṇasya vaktraṃ parijighramāṇā; rorūyate putravadhābhitaptā
english: Rolling on the earth and fallen down, then rising again, wretched, she kisses Karṇa's face and wails aloud, tormented by the slaying of her son.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca āvantyaṃ bhīmasenena bhakṣayanti nipātitam gṛdhragomāyavaḥ śūraṃ bahubandhum abandhuvat
english: Gāndhārī said: The vultures and jackals devour the Āvantya hero, struck down by Bhīmasena — he who had many kinsmen, now as though he had none.

sanskrit: taṃ paśya kadanaṃ kṛtvā śatrūṇāṃ madhusūdana śayānaṃ vīraśayane rudhireṇa samukṣitam
english: Behold him, O slayer of Madhu, who wrought havoc among his foes, now lying on the bed of heroes, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: taṃ sṛgālāś ca kaṅkāś ca kravyādāś ca pṛthagvidhāḥ tena tena vikarṣanti paśya kālasya paryayam
english: Jackals and herons and flesh-eaters of every kind drag him this way and that — behold the turning of Time.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ vīraśayane vīram ākrandasāriṇam āvantyam abhito nāryo rudatyaḥ paryupāsate
english: As he lies on the bed of heroes — that hero who pressed forward through the battle's din — the women sit weeping around the Āvantya on every side.

sanskrit: prātipīyaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ hataṃ bhallena bāhlikam prasuptam iva śārdūlaṃ paśya kṛṣṇa manasvinam
english: Behold the wise Bāhlika, descendant of Pratīpa, the mighty archer, slain by a broad-headed arrow, O Kṛṣṇa, like a tiger fallen fast asleep.

sanskrit: atīva mukhavarṇo 'sya nihatasyāpi śobhate somasyevābhipūrṇasya paurṇamāsyāṃ samudyataḥ
english: Even though he is slain, the color of his face shines exceedingly, like the full moon risen on the night of the full moon.

sanskrit: putraśokābhitaptena pratijñāṃ parirakṣatā pākaśāsaninā saṃkhye vārddhakṣatrir nipātitaḥ
english: Burning with grief for his son and keeping his vow, the son of the Chastiser of Pāka struck down in battle the son of Vṛddhakṣatra.

sanskrit: ekādaśa camūr jitvā rakṣyamāṇaṃ mahātmanā satyaṃ cikīrṣatā paśya hatam enaṃ jayadratham
english: Though guarded by that great soul who, having conquered eleven armies, sought to make his vow come true — behold this Jayadratha slain.

sanskrit: sindhusauvīrabhartāraṃ darpapūrṇaṃ manasvinam bhakṣayanti śivā gṛdhrā janārdana jayadratham
english: The jackals and vultures devour Jayadratha, lord of the Sindhus and the Sauvīras, full of pride and high of spirit, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣyamāṇaṃ bhāryābhir anuraktābhir acyuta bhaṣanto vyapakarṣanti gahanaṃ nimnam antikāt
english: Though guarded by his loving wives, O Acyuta, they snarl and drag him off from close at hand into a deep thicket.

sanskrit: tam etāḥ paryupāsante rakṣamāṇā mahābhujam sindhusauvīragāndhārakāmbojayavanastriyaḥ
english: These women sit about that mighty-armed one, guarding him — the women of the Sindhus, the Sauvīras, the Gāndhāras, the Kāmbojas, and the Yavanas.

sanskrit: yadā kṛṣṇām upādāya prādravat kekayaiḥ saha tadaiva vadhyaḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ janārdana jayadrathaḥ
english: From the very moment he seized Kṛṣṇā and fled with the Kekayas, Jayadratha was doomed to be slain by the Pāṇḍavas, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: duḥśalāṃ mānayadbhis tu yadā mukto jayadrathaḥ katham adya na tāṃ kṛṣṇa mānayanti sma te punaḥ
english: But when Jayadratha was let go out of regard for Duḥśalā, how is it, O Kṛṣṇa, that they did not again show her that same regard today?

sanskrit: saiṣā mama sutā bālā vilapantī suduḥkhitā pramāpayati cātmānam ākrośati ca pāṇḍavān
english: There is my young daughter, wailing in deepest grief, who would do herself to death and reviles the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu duḥkhataraṃ kṛṣṇa paraṃ mama bhaviṣyati yat sutā vidhavā bālā snuṣāś ca nihateśvarāḥ
english: What greater sorrow than this could befall me, O Kṛṣṇa — that my young daughter is widowed, and my daughters-in-law have lost their lords?

sanskrit: aho dhig duḥśalāṃ paśya vītaśokabhayām iva śiro bhartur anāsādya dhāvamānām itas tataḥ
english: Alas! Behold Duḥśalā, as though emptied of all grief and fear, running this way and that, not finding her husband's head.

sanskrit: vārayām āsa yaḥ sarvān pāṇḍavān putragṛddhinaḥ sa hatvā vipulāḥ senāḥ svayaṃ mṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: He who held off all the Pāṇḍavas, greedy for their sons' victory, having slain vast armies, has himself passed into the power of death.

sanskrit: taṃ mattam iva mātaṅgaṃ vīraṃ paramadurjayam parivārya rudanty etāḥ striyaś candropamānanāḥ
english: Around that hero, all but unconquerable, like a rutting elephant, these women with faces fair as the moon stand weeping.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca eṣa śalyo hataḥ śete sākṣān nakulamātulaḥ dharmajñena satā tāta dharmarājena saṃyuge
english: Gāndhārī said: Here lies Śalya slain, Nakula's own maternal uncle, O child, struck down in battle by the righteous, true-hearted Dharma-king.

sanskrit: yas tvayā spardhate nityaṃ sarvatra puruṣarṣabha sa eṣa nihataḥ śete madrarājo mahārathaḥ
english: He who ever contended with you in all things, O bull among men — there lies the king of the Madras, the great chariot-warrior, slain.

sanskrit: yena saṃgṛhṇatā tāta ratham ādhirather yudhi jayārthaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ tathā tejovadhaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: He who, taking the reins of the son of Adhiratha's chariot in battle, O child, thus brought low his splendor for the sake of the victory of Pāṇḍu's sons —

sanskrit: aho dhik paśya śalyasya pūrṇacandrasudarśanam mukhaṃ padmapalāśākṣaṃ vaḍair ādaṣṭam avraṇam
english: Alas! Behold Śalya's face, fair to look upon as the full moon, its eyes like lotus petals, pecked at by crows yet unwounded.

sanskrit: eṣā cāmīkarābhasya taptakāñcanasaprabhā āsyād viniḥsṛtā jihvā bhakṣyate kṛṣṇa pakṣibhiḥ
english: And the tongue of him whose hue was like gold, gleaming like refined gold, lolling out from his mouth, is being eaten by the birds, O Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhireṇa nihataṃ śalyaṃ samitiśobhanam rudantyaḥ paryupāsate madrarājakulastriyaḥ
english: Around Śalya, the ornament of the assembly, slain by Yudhiṣṭhira, the women of the house of the Madra king sit weeping.

sanskrit: etāḥ susūkṣmavasanā madrarājaṃ nararṣabham krośanty abhisamāsādya kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabham
english: These kṣatriya women in finest raiment, drawing near to the Madra king, that bull among men, that bull among kṣatriyas, cry aloud.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ nipatitaṃ nāryaḥ parivāryābhitaḥ sthitāḥ vāśitā gṛṣṭayaḥ paṅke parimagnam ivarṣabham
english: The women stand surrounding the fallen Śalya on every side, like lowing young cows around a bull sunk fast in the mire.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ śaraṇadaṃ śūraṃ paśyainaṃ rathasattamam śayānaṃ vīraśayane śarair viśakalīkṛtam
english: Behold this Śalya, the hero who granted refuge, that best of chariot-warriors, lying on the bed of heroes, torn to pieces by arrows.

sanskrit: eṣa śailālayo rājā bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān gajāṅkuśadharaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ śete bhuvi nipātitaḥ
english: Here lies the mighty King Bhagadatta, dweller in the mountains, foremost among wielders of the elephant-goad, struck down upon the earth.

sanskrit: yasya rukmamayī mālā śirasy eṣā virājate śvāpadair bhakṣyamāṇasya śobhayantīva mūrdhajān
english: Upon his head this garland of gold still gleams, seeming to adorn the hair of him whom the beasts of prey devour.

sanskrit: etena kila pārthasya yuddham āsīt sudāruṇam lomaharṣaṇam atyugraṃ śakrasya balinā yathā
english: With him, they say, Pārtha waged a most terrible battle, hair-raising and utterly fierce, like Śakra's war with Bali.

sanskrit: yodhayitvā mahābāhur eṣa pārthaṃ dhanaṃjayam saṃśayaṃ gamayitvā ca kuntīputreṇa pātitaḥ
english: This mighty-armed one, having given battle to Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya and brought him to the brink of doubt, was felled by the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: yasya nāsti samo loke śaurye vīrye ca kaś cana sa eṣa nihataḥ śete bhīṣmo bhīṣmakṛd āhave
english: He who has no equal in all the world for prowess and for valor — there lies Bhīṣma slain, who wrought terrible deeds in battle.
